definition: The radius of a nucleus, $R = R_0A^{\frac{1}{3}}$ with $R_0 = 1.20 \times 10^{-15}\ \text{m}$ and $A$ the nucleon number, so a nucleus's volume is proportional to $A$ and every nucleus has about the same density.

In a head-on collision, the distance between a charged particle and the centre of a nucleus at the instant the particle stops, when all its initial kinetic energy has become electric potential energy.

A model of the hydrogen atom in which the electron can only move in circular orbits whose angular momentum is $mvr = \frac{nh}{2\pi}$, which gives discrete energy levels $E = -\frac{13.6}{n^{2}}\ \text{eV}$.
